newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends sharply higher to limit up.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends sharply higher to limit up.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed sharply higher to limit up on cash-connected buying, analysts and traders said.

Selling by commodity funds had forced lumber futures sharply lower Wednesday and early Thursday. Commercial buying surfaced when that selling was completed. The buying found stiff seller resistance which drove bids and contract prices higher.

The lumber industry continues to await news from Canada regarding export quotas. But analysts and cash dealers were unaware of any such news from Canada ahead of the close to prompt the wave of cash-connected buying.
Lumber closed up $10.00 to $6.00 with November up $9.80 at $422.00 and January up the $10.00 limit at $384.40.
